objectives.en: Find magnifying power of simple and compound microscopes
Find magnifying power and length of a telescope

narration.en: Two lenses can show you a bacterium or the rings of Saturn. The microscope and the telescope use the same idea in opposite ways.
narration.kn: ಎರಡು ಮಸೂರಗಳು ಬ್ಯಾಕ್ಟೀರಿಯಾವನ್ನೂ ಶನಿಯ ಉಂಗುರಗಳನ್ನೂ ತೋರಿಸಬಲ್ಲವು. ಸೂಕ್ಷ್ಮದರ್ಶಕ ಮತ್ತು ದೂರದರ್ಶಕ ಒಂದೇ ತತ್ವವನ್ನು ವಿರುದ್ಧ ರೀತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಬಳಸುತ್ತವೆ.

body.en: A simple microscope is a convex lens held close to the eye. Its magnifying power is $m = 1 + D/f$ with the image at the near point ($D = 25$ cm) and $m = D/f$ with the image at infinity. A compound microscope has a short-focus objective that forms a real, magnified image, and an eyepiece that magnifies it further: $m \approx (L/f_o)(D/f_e)$, where $L$ is the tube length.
body.kn: ಸರಳ ಸೂಕ್ಷ್ಮದರ್ಶಕದ ವರ್ಧನಾ ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯ m = 1 + D/f (ಸಮೀಪ ಬಿಂದುವಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಬಿಂಬ). ಸಂಯುಕ್ತ ಸೂಕ್ಷ್ಮದರ್ಶಕದಲ್ಲಿ m ≈ (L/f_o)(D/f_e).

narration.en: A simple microscope is a convex lens held close to the eye. Its magnifying power is m = 1 + D/f with the image at the near point (D = 25 cm) and m = D/f with the image at infinity. A compound microscope has a short-focus objective that forms a real, magnified image, and an eyepiece that magnifies it further: m \approx (L/f_o)(D/f_e), where L is the tube length.
narration.kn: ಸರಳ ಸೂಕ್ಷ್ಮದರ್ಶಕದ ವರ್ಧನಾ ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯ m = 1 + D/f (ಸಮೀಪ ಬಿಂದುವಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಬಿಂಬ). ಸಂಯುಕ್ತ ಸೂಕ್ಷ್ಮದರ್ಶಕದಲ್ಲಿ m ≈ (L/f_o)(D/f_e).

narration.en: Let us sketch a compound microscope and a telescope and find their magnifying powers.

say.en: A compound microscope: a short-focus objective makes a real, enlarged first image; the eyepiece magnifies it further, like a simple magnifier.
The magnification is the objective's times the eyepiece's. With L = 15 cm, f_o = 2 cm and f_e = 5 cm, m is about 37.5.
A telescope: a long-focus objective forms an image of a distant object at its focus; the eyepiece views it. In normal adjustment the tube length is f_o + f_e.
The angular magnification is f_o over f_e. With f_o = 100 cm and f_e = 5 cm, m = 20 and the tube is 105 cm long.

narration.en: Parallel light from a distant star is focused by the objective (focal length fo) to an image at its focus. The eyepiece (fe) acts as a magnifier. In normal adjustment the final rays come out parallel and M = fo/fe, tube length fo + fe. With the final image at 25 cm, M = (fo/fe)(1 + fe/25). Angles are exaggerated.

caption.en: Parallel light from a distant star is focused by the objective (focal length fo) to an image at its focus. The eyepiece (fe) acts as a magnifier. In normal adjustment the final rays come out parallel and M = fo/fe, tube length fo + fe. With the final image at 25 cm, M = (fo/fe)(1 + fe/25). Angles are exaggerated.
caption.kn: ದೂರದ ನಕ್ಷತ್ರದ ಸಮಾಂತರ ಬೆಳಕನ್ನು ವಸ್ತು ಮಸೂರ (fo) ತನ್ನ ನಾಭಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಬಿಂಬವಾಗಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ನೇತ್ರ ಮಸೂರ (fe) ವರ್ಧಕದಂತೆ. ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ಹೊಂದಾಣಿಕೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಅಂತಿಮ ಕಿರಣಗಳು ಸಮಾಂತರ, M = fo/fe, ನಳಿಕೆ ಉದ್ದ fo + fe. ಅಂತಿಮ ಬಿಂಬ 25 cm ನಲ್ಲಿದ್ದರೆ M = (fo/fe)(1 + fe/25).

body.en: An astronomical telescope has a long-focus objective and a short-focus eyepiece. In normal adjustment (final image at infinity) its magnifying power is $m = f_o/f_e$ and its length is $f_o + f_e$. Reflecting telescopes use a concave mirror as the objective: there is no chromatic aberration, a paraboloid mirror removes spherical aberration, and a large mirror is easier to support than a large lens.
body.kn: ಖಗೋಳ ದೂರದರ್ಶಕದಲ್ಲಿ m = f_o/f_e ಮತ್ತು ಉದ್ದ f_o + f_e. ಪ್ರತಿಫಲಕ ದೂರದರ್ಶಕದಲ್ಲಿ ವರ್ಣ ವಿಪಥನ ಇಲ್ಲ.

points.en: Large objective aperture gives better resolution and brightness

narration.en: An astronomical telescope has a long-focus objective and a short-focus eyepiece. body.en: Microscope: both lenses short. Telescope: objective long, eyepiece short. If you remember that m grows when the eyepiece focal length is small, you have both.
